reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) comes entirely from a study on equiatomic CrNiFeCoMn, not the Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy in the hypothesis. While the general phenomena of nitride/σ precipitation and property degradation are shown for the Cantor alloy, the hypothesis assumes without direct support that the same phases, temperature ranges, and failure mechanisms apply to a chemically distinct AM HEA containing Al and Ti, which are strong nitride/formers and can alter phase stability.
premises: As-produced AM Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA contains fine nitride and σ phase precipitates
These precipitates grow and increase in number during annealing at 900–1300 K
σ phase preferentially locates at grain boundaries above ~950 K
Precipitate evolution reduces mechanical properties and can cause catastrophic failure
The cited evidence on equiatomic CrNiFeCoMn directly applies to the non-equiatomic Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy
